chunks: My father, (Radwanullah) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ali ibn Isma'il from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abu Ayyub from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his forefathers (peace be upon them), from Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said:
The longest among you in Qunoot in the abode of the world, the longest among you in peace on the Day of Resurrection in the Standing (Place).
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for long Qunoot in prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-A'mal, Shaykh al-Saduq narrates this hadith via a strong chain to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.), emphasizing that the length of one's Qunoot (often interpreted as the standing in prayer or specific supplications) serves as a direct metric for one's comfort and ease (raha) during the intense Standing (Mauqif) on the Day of Judgment. This links the physical discipline of worship in the dunya to the spiritual tranquility in the akhirah, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the transformative power of sustained devotion.
